Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

knowledge (development version)

  • knw_tune_run() gains grid_args, passed to knw_tune_grid(), and reads a cached score back only for the grid it was scored on (#67). scripts/0322 scored chinook rearing on gradient limits up to 30 %: the best rule moves from 9 % to 15 %, and every limit from 7 to 30 % has rules in the region, but choosing among the longer ladder loses to default under nested selection. CH_rear_v1 keeps 9 %; extending the ladder for every species is #68. The chinook rearing article says so.

knowledge 0.4.4

  • A pkgdown article, vignette("chinook_rearing"), explains in plain language how the chinook rearing threshold was chosen from the province’s electrofishing records and what it changes on link’s segments, with a Bulkley map, a zoom and three labelled example segments (#62). Its data are written by data-raw/vignette_chinook.R to inst/vignette-data/, and a test fails when a tracked source moves on. knw_compare_map() gains ncol, panels, mark, lwd, legend and labels; its default output is unchanged. The package now declares R >= 4.1.0.

knowledge 0.4.3

  • One evidence build, one tuning run and one comparison across species and life stages, as package functions on link’s province-wide default run (#57): knw_fdis_visits(), knw_link_place(), knw_link_flow(), knw_link_width(), knw_link_walks(), knw_link_barrier_dnstr(), knw_bcfishobs_match() and knw_link_access_check() build the evidence; knw_tune_grid(), knw_tune_score(), knw_tune_curve(), knw_grade() and knw_tune_run() score every rule of each species and stage on held-out watershed groups, pick, fit the joint curve and grade every segment; knw_thresholds_table() and knw_publish() write the thresholds and grade tables; knw_compare_rules(), knw_floodplain_ha() and knw_compare_map() show what a rule changes on link’s segments (km, graded km, floodplain hectares, maps). Scripts 0300–0330 run them.
  • Eight species × stage fit. default is outside the one-SE region for every species but grayling; chinook’s size floor settles at 0.75 m³/s; bull trout spawning fits but is weak. data/thresholds.csv and data/thresholds_groups.csv carry the result in link’s parameter names; 0290, 0294 and 0296 write their tables from the new build, and 0291–0298 read the published v2 visit tables (0299 PULL=TRUE VERSION=v2). Results: research/habitat_thresholds_tuned.md and one file per species.

knowledge 0.4.2

  • The README points at the published FDIS visit tables’ second release, knowledge/fdis/v2/, which keeps one copy of a survey loaded under several collection ids and carries the crosswalk from v1’s site_visit ids (#35).

knowledge 0.4.1

  • The package now sits at the repository root and installs with pak::pak("NewGraphEnvironment/knowledge"). DESCRIPTION gains URL (the new pkgdown site and the repository) and BugReports, and the knw_pscis_pull() example connects through the standard PG* environment variables.

knowledge 0.4.0

  • New evidence variable instream_flow: a flow need, the water a life stage needs while it is in the stream, kept apart from discharge, which is stream size (usually the MAD an intrinsic-potential model filters on). It takes m3/s, cfs, percent MAD, a percentile or a percent exceedance, and a metric naming the flow statistic it is held to (instantaneous, daily_mean, 7day_low, monthly_mean, monthly_median, unstated). It carries no parameter or model_id, and the *_mad_* parameters now sit on discharge rows only. A 7day_low row needs a note giving its return period.
  • depth and velocity read in the unit the source wrote: cm and ft for depth, cm/s and ft/s for velocity, as well as m and m/s. A channel’s bankfull depth is stream size and reads as m bankfull.
  • Rows that changed variable or unit, so a filter on the old values returns fewer rows: data row 121 (a migration low flow, now instream_flow and coded SALMON), rows 250, 257 and 264 (bankfull depths, now m bankfull), and rows 497 and 498 (redd velocities, now cm/s as quoted).

knowledge 0.3.1

  • New evidence variable groundwater: upwelling, hyporheic exchange and springs. It takes no unit, so a groundwater row is a statement with no value, until a source gives an upwelling measure.

knowledge 0.3.0

  • knw_literature_read() requires a metric column, after unit: which statistic a temperature value is (daily maximum, MWMT, 7DADM, MWAT, 7DEC, a weekly, monthly, August, summer or annual mean, a constant laboratory exposure, or unstated), or which window a degree-day total accumulates over (growing_season, to_hatch, to_emergence, annual). A table without the column is refused. A temperature-family value needs a metric that fits its variable; a none row may name the one it searched for; every other row leaves it blank.
  • New evidence variables degree_days (degC-day) and air_temperature (degC). Air temperature is its own variable because intrinsic-potential models use it as a proxy for water temperature. A cited degree_days row needs a note giving its base temperature.
  • A none row may carry bound, naming the limit that was searched for.
  • New kind lab: a laboratory or hatchery measurement (a lethal limit, CTmax, survival or growth at held temperatures, a development time in degree-days), which is not expert opinion.
  • A qual row is refused a value: it is a statement, and a value on it would be counted as evidence it is not.

knowledge 0.2.1

  • knw_literature_vocab() adds elevation to the variable vocabulary, in m or ft, so a source that fits an elevation term (a watershed-scale occurrence coefficient, say) can be recorded. Other units are refused.

knowledge 0.2.0

  • knw_ip_read() and knw_ip_vocab() read and validate the intrinsic-potential model registry: one row per model, species and life stage, recording how the model sizes streams (flow_metric, flow_source, flow_inputs, flow_surrogate), its valley-confinement variable and whether it was validated against fish, each claim with a verbatim quote.
  • knw_literature_read() requires a model_id column (its value may be blank), linking a threshold to the registry model that uses it. A table without the column is refused.
  • parameter is now a controlled vocabulary (the habitat-model parameter names, in knw_literature_vocab()), so a misspelt or invented parameter is refused rather than silently matching nothing.
  • New evidence variables valley_width_index (ratio) and drainage_area (km2, mi2); cfs for discharge and ft for channel width are read as the source wrote them.

knowledge 0.1.0

  • First version: PSCIS pulls by watershed group, GNIS collision checks, size classes, and readers for the life-history timing and literature evidence tables.
